techStack: React 19.0.0 with automatic JSX transform (react-jsx) — no 'import React' needed
TypeScript ~5.7.2; verbatimModuleSyntax: true — type-only imports must use 'import type'
Plain CSS only — no CSS Modules, no Tailwind; src/styles/style.css EXISTS, src/styles.css does NOT
noUnusedLocals and noUnusedParameters enforced — unused vars are errors
strict mode not globally set, but individual strict flags active
features: Product type (src/types/product.ts): field is 'discountPct?: number' — no 'discountPercent' field exists
ProductCard.tsx: references product.discountPercent at 3 sites (lines 9, 25, 37) — all must become product.discountPct
SortSelect.tsx: passes e.target.value (string) directly to onChange which expects FilterState['sortBy'] union — type mismatch
App.tsx line 2: imports './styles.css' — file does not exist; should be './styles/style.css'
App.tsx: <ProductList products={visibleProducts}> is not self-closed — missing '/>' causes JSX parse error
formatters.ts formatPrice(price, discountPct?) uses 'discountPct' naming — consistent with type
data/products.ts uses 'discountPct' correctly on sample products (products 4, 7, 13)
architecture: src/ tree: App.tsx, main.tsx, api/, components/, data/, hooks/, styles/, types/, utils/
src/styles/style.css exists and is the correct target for the CSS import fix
All imports use relative paths only — no aliases (@/, ~) configured in tsconfig or vite.config
Tests live under tests/ at project root (not src/tests/) — must not be modified per constraints
tsconfig.app.json includes both 'src' and 'tests' directories for type-checking
No monorepo wrapper — benchmark-frontend is a standalone pnpm package
edgeCases: discountPct is optional (?: number) — hasDiscount guard in ProductCard must use discountPct so products without discount render correctly (no undefined badge)
<ProductList /> self-close must retain products={visibleProducts} prop — omitting it would silence the product grid and fail sorting tests
Type cast in SortSelect must be 'as FilterState['sortBy']', NOT 'as any' — no-any is required per project TypeScript standard
No tests directly assert on discount display — discountPct rename fix is driven by TypeScript build error, not test failure
Sort tests (sorting.test.tsx) compare h3 heading arrays by product name — would catch a missing products prop on ProductList indirectly
app.render.test.tsx and pagination.test.tsx would fail if App.tsx JSX parse error is not fixed (app won't render at all)
verbatimModuleSyntax: true — if FilterState is only used as a type in SortSelect, its import must use 'import type'
